A1.justification: Both complete 33-page PDFs describe the same AttWarp research. Text and rendered-page comparisons cover the main paper and Appendices A–I; the only visible difference is the first-page arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original AttWarp benchmark experiments in Table 1, plus ablations, robustness studies, localization experiments and distribution analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the five-benchmark comparison in Table 1 and the open-vocabulary object detection experiment in Table 16.

M1.justification: The rectilinear warping procedure, AttWarp-Chain stopping rule, AttWarp-Distill architecture and loss, attention aggregation, and appendix adaptations are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions use TextVQA, GQA, DocVQA, POPE and MMMU, with the same appendix coverage of gRef multi-object queries, open-vocabulary object detection, corrupted images and adversarial inputs.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same base models and FGVP-mask, FGVP-blur, SoM, API and ViCrop comparators. Comparator membership also matches throughout the appendix experiments and non-rectilinear warping comparison.

E3.justification: Evaluation protocols and settings are identical, including dataset splits, model configurations, metrics and training budgets. Appendix G retains the 336×336 LLaVA and 512×512 Qwen input settings.

E4.justification: The same layer, head-aggregation, transform, feature-space, corruption and adversarial studies remain in Appendix B. Error analysis, chain-depth analysis, external-attention experiments, localization studies and distribution-shift analyses are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical, including Table 3's head-resampling note and Appendix I's estimation descriptions. No run-count, seed, uncertainty-interval or significance-reporting information is added or removed.

E6.justification: Tables 1–16, plots and qualitative outcomes are unchanged. For example, both report LLaVA TextVQA accuracy of 49.3% for the base model and 58.1% with AttWarp, and Table 16 reports 54.0% versus 61.0% for original versus warped OVOD inputs.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 and the appendices' diagonal-Jacobian reasoning, Mahalanobis formulation and distributional assumptions are identical. No mathematical definitions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about attention-guided input warping, preservation of global context, plug-and-play compatibility and improvements across five benchmarks and four MLLMs.

C2.justification: Both retain the same attention-redistribution and distribution-preservation explanations, together with limitations involving noisy attention, peripheral context, size comparisons and excessive iterative warping.

D1.justification: Appendix G contains identical implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, preprocessing and computational-cost information. Project/code links and the promise to release code, configurations and analysis scripts are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, citations throughout the paper and the reference list are identical. Positioning relative to visual prompting, attention refinement and earlier image-warping methods is unchanged.

P1.justification: Only the marginal arXiv stamp changes from v1, 10 Oct 2025, to v2, 11 Feb 2026. The title, authors, prose, terminology, section structure and appendix organization are identical.

P2.justification: All figures, tables, captions and page arrangements are unchanged. Rendered pages match outside the updated first-page version/date text; no visual material is added, removed or relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 reproduces v1's scientific content, results, explanations and reproducibility information throughout the main paper and Appendices A–I. Updating the arXiv stamp and corresponding self-link/metadata produces no meaningful gain or loss in overall paper quality.
